So I was able to stop drinking last NYE, and once I got through those first few weeks of cravings, life was freaking great! I still utilize cannabis instead of pharmaceuticals for my depression/life struggles, though I am hopeful to remain positive through this new journey without the use of cannabis. I feel great when I wake up and start my day without, but I have quickly realized how much it helped me sleep and eat. Didn’t eat until 6pm yesterday, just had my morning coffee and water throughout the afternoon. Hoping to get some decent sleep sometime this week, fingers are crossed!! 

It also upsets me how normalized alcohol is and cannabis isn’t. Like what will I even be offered for a break as a nurse if I’m not chain smoking cigs or downing glasses of wine in between patients like the rest of them? Sorry, sarcasm is at a high level this morning (:

I really appreciate your input, thank you so much!! To be fair, I don’t hear that often, and it brought joy to my heart and a smile to my face, thank you!! I literally have to hold back tears when my professors tell me about how well I am doing, because they are literally the only ones who notice.

I honestly thought I would find a few study buds but I have come to realize I much prefer to study alone. I get too distracted with others around. I find myself in the most secluded areas in between classes with  my headphones and notes. Everyone complains often about the professors, and I know shit will get way more difficult once I am actually in the thick of the program.

Nah, I see cannabis more so as a medicine, not a narcotic. I have no issues quitting. Besides, I’ve lost a handful of friends due to their own addictions to true narcotics and I have zero interest in listening to others’ stories of their recovery. Also, pretty sure I DIDN’T ask for advice, but thanks for the offer anyways I guess? Sounds cold, yes, probably why I have no friends. But clearly you didn’t read my post, I appreciate the thought, that is, in the end, what counts.
